title: First direct decoding of full words from the cortex of a paralyzed, anarthric man (UCSF, BRAVO trial)
summary: 128-electrode ECoG and deep-learning decoder let a man mute since 2003 produce sentences at 15.2 wpm from a 50-word vocabulary
account: At the University of California, San Francisco, a 36-year-old man received a 128-electrode subdural electrocorticography array over sensorimotor cortex in the BRAVO trial (NCT03698149). He had anarthria and severe spastic quadriparesis from an extensive pontine stroke at age 20 and is known in press by the pseudonym Pancho. Deep-learning models detected his attempted speech and classified words from a 50-word vocabulary, with a natural-language model and Viterbi decoder assembling sentences. He produced sentences at a median 15.2 words per minute with a median word error rate of 25.6%. He previously typed about five words per minute with a head-controlled pointer (Moses et al., NEJM, 15 July 2021). The paper dates implantation to February 2019 and the start of data collection to April 2019. There were 50 sessions over 81 weeks at the participant's residence or a nearby office. The session on which the reported sentence decoding was achieved is not dated. So the start of data collection (1 April 2019) is used as the observation date.
purpose: Built to decode attempted speech into words and sentences for a person with anarthria. Restoring word-level communication was the intended benefit and is what occurred.
model_version: 128-electrode high-density ECoG array (16-by-8 lattice, 4 mm spacing); deep-learning speech-detection and word-classification models with natural-language model and Viterbi decoder; 50-word vocabulary

ratings.reason: Material benefit to one identifiable person: first decoding of his own full words, three times faster than his pointer typing. But limited to a 50-word vocabulary in research sessions.

ai_role.statement: Deep-learning models detected attempted speech in 98% of attempts and classified words. A language model with Viterbi decoding assembled sentences. The output depended entirely on these models. Funding included a research contract under Facebook's Sponsored Academic Research Agreement. The paper states that no study hardware or data were transferred to any sponsor and that author disclosure forms are available at NEJM.org.
